After two years of silence, Apple is developing a brand-new iMac powered by the M6 chip and featuring fresh colour options, according to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman. The new machine will arrive "before the end of the year."

iMac refresh cycles have always been infrequent. The lineup skipped both the M2 and M5 chip generations, and a larger-screen version has never materialised—instead, Apple has steered power users toward pairing a Mac Studio or Mac mini with a Studio Display. Even so, the company is preparing a new model with the M6 chip.

Gurman hinted that this update will bring "some new colour options," but stopped short of specifying the changes. Apple made subtle colour adjustments with the 2024 M4 refresh, keeping the original seven colours but shifting the tones slightly. The new iMac is expected to launch before year-end as well:

All of this suggests that this autumn could be a significant quarter for the Mac. On the agenda: a completely redesigned MacBook Pro with a touchscreen and Tandem OLED; a new 14-inch MacBook Pro with the M6 chip; a new Mac Studio with M5 Max and M5 Ultra (supply permitting); and a new iMac with the M6. Another possibility is an updated Mac mini with M6 and M5 Pro options, though that is expected to arrive later.

Apple's M6 chip will be the first Mac processor built on an all-new 2nm process, but reportedly there will be no M6 Pro, M6 Max, or M6 Ultra variants—instead, Apple will accelerate the rollout of the M7 series.
